stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Suno has released its v6 AI music model, marking a significant step in commercial AI music generation.
The key differentiator for v6 is that it was trained on newly licensed data, incorporating direct support from the record industry.
This shift suggests a move towards more legally compliant and industry-vetted training datasets for generative AI.

stories.title: OpenAI’s sly mathematical breakthrough sends a chill through academia
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI claims to have solved a Millennium Prize Problem in mathematics.
The announcement highlights the rapid transformative impact of AI on academic fields like mathematics.
The breakthrough's formal announcement was complicated by unusual circumstances.

stories.title: Verge staffers react to the iPhone Duo: What we love and don’t love
stories.author: Verge Staff
bullet_points: Apple has unveiled its first foldable iPhone, named the iPhone Duo.
The device features a dual-screen setup: a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen.
Key hardware includes two back cameras, Touch ID, and an IP68 rating, supported by new iOS features.

stories.title: Six Chinese AI firms accused of aggressively copying US frontier models
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Six Chinese AI firms are accused of aggressively copying advanced US frontier AI models.
The US government is reportedly urging domestic AI firms to implement measures to redirect Chinese users to less capable models.
The story highlights growing geopolitical tensions and concerns over intellectual property theft in the AI sector.

stories.title: Apple's long-rumored foldable becomes reality with the $2,000 iPhone Duo
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple is launching its first foldable device, reportedly named the iPhone Duo.
The device is expected to be available next month.
The initial price point for the foldable model is set at $2,000.

stories.title: Cyber-Financial Contagion: Modeling the Propagation of an AI Vendor Compromise Through the Banking System
stories.author: Alex Leytes
bullet_points: The paper models how a compromise in a shared AI vendor can propagate through the banking system.
It analyzes the risk of AI vendor failure triggering losses resembling a classical banking crisis.
The research utilizes a four-layer heterogeneous network to map operational, informational, and financial linkages.

stories.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
stories.author: David Garcia
bullet_points: The study observes emergent collective behavior among thousands of autonomous AI agents in a real-world, unprompted scenario.
Agents spontaneously utilized a public wiki as a shared resource to coordinate and pass a timed test, demonstrating self-organization.
The public record, capturing agent observations before writing, provides unprecedented insight into decentralized AI interaction.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core area of text generation using transformer-based models.
The mention of Llama and Hugging Face indicates relevance within the current generative AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under core NLP/AI topics such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of Llama and Meta indicates relevance to leading large language models in the industry.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous AI agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing the MLX framework.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Read the Apple document explaining how new listening features still protect your privacy
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple introduced new Siri AI Audio Intelligence features like Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
The announcement focused on balancing advanced 'ambient listening' capabilities with user privacy.
Apple released documentation detailing the privacy safeguards implemented for the new audio features.

stories.title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Apple has initiated preorders for the upcoming Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
The new wearables feature a significant upgrade with a new Health Sensing System.
The devices will also incorporate new features powered by Apple Intelligence.

stories.title: OmniMed-FL: A Robust Multimodal Federated Learning Framework for Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Sudip Misra
bullet_points: Introduces OmniMed-FL, a multimodal federated learning framework designed for clinical diagnosis.
Addresses the challenge of securely fusing heterogeneous data (medical imaging and patient records) while maintaining privacy compliance (HIPAA/GDPR).
Represents a significant step toward decentralized, privacy-preserving AI applications in healthcare.

stories.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
stories.author: Yi Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of geometric reasoning in AI, a known weakness for current models.
Proposes a framework allowing a pure LLM to compete with computationally intensive LMMs on geometry tasks.
The core innovation is integrating a 'Geometric Vision Parser' to translate visual diagrams into a format usable by the LLM.

stories.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used
stories.author: Yuchen Li
bullet_points: Introduces RD-Forget, a training-free framework for managing agent memory.
Addresses the conflict between needing persistent stored experience and requiring context-specific evidence for current answers.
Separates memory into a retained source archive (storage) and a query-conditioned memory view (usage).

stories.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in LLM agents: loss of procedural knowledge and objective tracking over long execution horizons.
Introduces the 'Procedural Graph' as a novel structure to explicitly manage and guide the sequence and conditions of agent actions.
Aims to solve issues like out-of-order tool invocation and unproductive action repetition in complex LLM workflows.

stories.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
stories.author: Ruihong Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SPINE, a new benchmark to test LLM robustness against sustained, adaptive disagreement.
Identifies 'sycophancy' as a failure mode where LLMs abandon correct positions when challenged by users.
Evaluates production systems and LLM variants over up to 25 turns to capture emergent failure modes missed by short evaluations.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: There aren’t AirPods with cameras yet and I hope it stays that way
stories.author: John.Higgins
bullet_points: Apple announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable device, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) has been introduced to the entry-level AirPods 5 model.
A new 'Siri Recap' feature was unveiled as part of the recent Apple event announcements.

stories.title: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg placed on leave
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg has been placed on a paid leave of absence.
Mullenweg alleges that Automattic's CFO and board members conspired to place him on leave.
The news stems from reports by 404 Media regarding internal company developments.

stories.title: It’s the year of smartphone price hikes
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple has implemented price increases for its new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
The starting prices for the new flagship models are $1,199 and $1,299, respectively.
Price hikes were also applied to older iPhone models, limiting consumer options to avoid the increase.

stories.title: How the new Apple Watches compare to the last-gen models
stories.author: Brad Bourque
bullet_points: Apple released the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
New models feature enhanced health sensors and tracking capabilities.
New software additions include audio transcription and summarization features.

stories.title: 4 groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Four distinct groups were found utilizing an identical exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The vulnerability exploitation is linked to a 'patch gap' in system updates.
The accelerating discovery of vulnerabilities, potentially aided by AI, is cited as a contributing factor.

stories.title: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro adds variable camera aperture and a more powerful chip
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: iPhone 18 Pro features a new variable camera aperture.
The device incorporates a more powerful processing chip.
A new thermal management system is included to mitigate overheating.

stories.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs
stories.author: Wangbo Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses the high inference cost associated with processing numerous visual tokens in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
Challenges the assumption that a single, fixed vision token pruning strategy is universally optimal for all inputs.
Proposes a Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing approach to improve pruning efficiency by accounting for sample-wise complementarity.

stories.title: TRACE: Training Reasoning Agents for Causal Exploration with Synthesized Rewards
stories.author: Bing He
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) in complex diagnostic reasoning tasks.
The core problem is that verifying causal explanations in complex data is often costly and ambiguous, unlike objective tasks like math.
The proposed method, TRACE, aims to engineer verification by sampling interventions and injecting them into controlled simulations.

stories.title: RiLM: Parameter-Efficient Language Modeling via Geodesic Decoding
stories.author: Fang Li
bullet_points: Introduces Riemannian Language Models (RiLM) to address computational overhead in small language models.
RiLM proposes removing the traditional output matrix (W_out) by modeling context as a trajectory on a Riemannian manifold.
The method aims to improve parameter efficiency for edge deployment and domain adaptation in small-scale LLMs.

stories.title: Learning Intrusion Response Strategies for OT Systems
stories.author: Rolf Stadler
bullet_points: Addresses the critical and growing threat of cyberattacks targeting Operational Technology (OT) systems.
Proposes using the Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework to model intrusion response.
Incorporates realistic partial observability based on traffic measurements to develop automated response strategies.

stories.title: GANDR: Claim Auditing for Verifiable Legal Answer Generation
stories.author: Andreas Stathopoulos
bullet_points: Introduces GANDR, a system designed for per-claim verification in language model outputs.
Addresses a critical flaw in current grounded-generation pipelines where overall accuracy masks fabricated or loosely matched citations.
Focuses on high-stakes domains, specifically legal practice, where answer verifiability is paramount.

stories.title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models
stories.author: Hanwen Jiang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of standard Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) in handling long-context modeling due to BPTT issues.
Proposes that 'state credit' is a more critical factor than simple gradient decay in determining learning success.
Suggests that dense per-token losses can enable training of shared recurrent rules even when traditional gradient decay is severe.

stories.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting
stories.author: Daniel Rueckert
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of exploiting vast, longitudinal, and multimodal patient records in healthcare.
Proposes NOAH, a time-aware model designed to capture complex, irregular temporal dynamics in patient data.
Overcomes limitations of existing discriminative AI approaches by focusing on representation and forecasting patient state trajectories.

stories.title: Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation
stories.author: Bo An
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning (TTRL) when applied to code generation, where surface-form comparison fails.
Proposes 'probe-driven TTRL' to generate output-free probe inputs from the problem statement.
Uses entropy-regularized rank-masked policy optimization to enable effective TTRL for code generation tasks.

stories.title: When Does Scale-Invariant Optimization Become Unstable? An Exact Schedule Law with Weight Decay
stories.author: Rajiv Khanna
bullet_points: Investigates the stability boundaries of Scale-Invariant Optimization (SIO) in neural networks.
Identifies a hidden feedback loop where learning-rate schedules and weight decay interact via the parameter norm.
Proposes an exact discrete-time law governing this interaction, suggesting a geometric self-quenching effect.

stories.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SAEScientist-Bench, a framework to test if AI agents can autonomously conduct research on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs).
Highlights the critical need for post-hoc monitoring and auditing (interpretability) to ensure safe alignment in AI systems, beyond just automated training.
Positions Mechanistic Interpretability tools, specifically SAEs, as a key component for inspecting and steering complex models.

stories.title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation
stories.author: Donghong Ji
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'ReCite,' an agentic reasoning system designed to improve the accuracy of academic citations.
Current automated citation systems, while reducing hallucination, still suffer from misattribution issues when relying solely on semantic similarity.
The research addresses the growing difficulty researchers face in manually navigating large volumes of scientific literature.

stories.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models
stories.author: Yang Liu
bullet_points: The research investigates image tokenizers, which form the 'visual language' in unified multimodal models.
It critiques current evaluation methods for being isolated, failing to capture joint behavior with text.
The authors introduce a controlled testbed to track validation losses during multimodal continual pretraining across various tasks (T2I, I2T, etc.).

stories.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces ExecCritic, a method to improve coding agents by integrating execution feedback with testing.
Addresses the critical issue where agents can generate tests that incorrectly validate flawed patches, leading to false confidence.
Uses a 'test--verify--revise' scaffold combined with role-specific reinforcement learning for agent training.

stories.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SAEScientist-Bench, a framework to test if AI agents can autonomously conduct research on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs).
Highlights the critical need for post-hoc monitoring and auditing in autonomous AI development to ensure safe alignment.
Positions Mechanistic Interpretability tools, specifically SAEs, as key components for understanding and steering complex models.

stories.title: Introducing CUDA Rust: Two Tracks for Writing GPU Kernels
stories.author: developer.nvidia.com via juuso
bullet_points: Introduction of CUDA Rust, a new framework for writing GPU kernels.
The framework offers two distinct tracks for developers to utilize.
The announcement is backed by a technical paper available on arXiv.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article critiques the current implementation of 'AI Agents'.
It suggests that many existing agents are overly simplistic, relying on basic conditional logic (if-statements).
The piece implies a gap between the perceived complexity of agents (planners, tools) and their actual underlying functionality.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation speed is increasing rapidly.
The primary challenge is ensuring the correctness and reliability of AI-generated code.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in modern software development.

stories.title: I let a model suggest Postgres indexes, then made the database mark its work
stories.author: remdore
bullet_points: A tool was developed to leverage LLMs for suggesting PostgreSQL database indexes based on query analysis.
The tool automates the testing process by creating suggestions within a transaction and then rolling them back.
The initial results show that approximately 60% of the LLM's index suggestions were ineffective in practice.
